syllabusTopics: Logic and set: statements, logical connectives, truth tables, theorems based on set operations
Real numbers: geometric representation of real numbers, interval, absolute value
Function: domain and range of a function, inverse function, composite function; algebraic (linear, quadratic and cubic) and transcendental (trigonometric, exponential, logarithmic) functions

Curve sketching: odd and even functions, periodicity, symmetry (about origin, X- and Y-axis), monotonicity; graphs of quadratic, cubic and rational functions, trigonometric (asinbx and acosbx), exponential (e^x), logarithmic (lnx)
Sequence and series: arithmetic, geometric, harmonic sequences and series and their properties; A.M, G.M, H.M and their relations; sum of infinite geometric series
Matrices and determinants: transpose of a matrix and its properties; minors and cofactors, adjoint, inverse matrix, determinant, properties of determinants (without proof)
Quadratic equation: nature and roots of a quadratic equation, relation between roots and coefficient, formation of a quadratic equation, symmetric roots, one or both roots common
Complex number: imaginary unit, algebra of complex numbers, geometric representation, absolute (modulus) value and conjugate of complex numbers and their properties, square root of a complex number

card.title: Quadratic equations — discriminant first, roots second

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: A quadratic ax² + bx + c = 0 has its fate sealed by the discriminant D = b² − 4ac before any solving: D > 0 gives two real (rational if D is a perfect square), D = 0 a repeated root, D < 0 a conjugate-complex pair. Roots and coefficients are locked together (sum = −b/a, product = c/a), so equations can be BUILT from roots, common-root conditions tested, and symmetric expressions evaluated without solving.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: x = [−b ± √(b²−4ac)] / 2a  ·  D = b² − 4ac: >0 real distinct · =0 equal · <0 complex conjugate  ·  α+β = −b/a, αβ = c/a  ·  build: x² − (sum)x + product = 0  ·  x²−5x+6 = 0 → x = 2, 3

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: a ≠ 0 (else it collapses to linear). Rational-root hunting (factor theorem) works over integers/rationals; irrational and complex roots need the formula. Common-root questions demand satisfying BOTH equations simultaneously. Complex roots of real-coefficient quadratics always pair conjugately.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: x² − 5x + 6 = 0 factors to (x−2)(x−3) → x = 2, 3 (NEB 2024). Symmetric sums (α²+β², 1/α+1/β) rewrite via (α+β) and αβ — never solve first. Equal-roots condition (D = 0) finds unknown coefficients; common root: subtract the equations to linearise.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Solve x² − 5x + 6 = 0: D = 25 − 24 = 1 > 0 (two real, rational). Factor: need two numbers ×6, +5 → 2 and 3 → (x−2)(x−3) = 0 → x = 2 or 3 (NEB 2024, 2 marks). Matrix companion from the same bank: det[[2,1],[3,4]] = 8−3 = 5; A⁻¹ = (1/5)[[4,−1],[−3,2]] (NEB 2023, 3 marks).

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: The formula solves quadratics only — cubics need other machinery. D classifies over the complexes; 'no real roots' still means two complex ones. Root-coefficient relations assume the STANDARD form (divide through by a first). Factoring works cleanly only for rational roots.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Complete the square: ax²+bx+c = a[(x + b/2a)² − (b²−4ac)/4a²] = 0 → (x + b/2a)² = D/4a² → the quadratic formula, with D's sign deciding root nature. Sum/product follow by comparing a(x−α)(x−β) = ax² − a(α+β)x + aαβ against ax²+bx+c term by term.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Compute D FIRST — it halves the work (and answers 'nature of roots' alone). Integer constant term? Try factor pairs before the formula. Formation: x² − Sx + P = 0 straight from sum/product. Matrices: 2×2 inverse = swap diagonal, negate off-diagonal, ÷det.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: NEB 2024 (2): solve x² − 5x + 6 = 0. NEB 2023 (3): sets A∪B/A∩B/A−B for {1,2,3},{2,3,4}. NEB 2023 (3): det + inverse of [[2,1],[3,4]]. Nature-of-roots and common-root conditions rotate yearly.
